decisions.choice: Yahweh spoke to Moses: a new speech in the instructions given on the mountain
decisions.reason: Since 25:1 Moses has been on the mountain receiving the plan of the tabernacle (24:18). A new speech begins here and names the workers who will build it.

decisions.choice: "parla", "dit" (passé simple, L and B); "a dit" (passé composé, R); the instructions that follow: future at L and B, imperative or "doit" at R
decisions.reason: The narrative frame follows the French style guide: passé simple at Literal and Balanced, passé composé at Readable. The instructions use the future of command at Literal and Balanced and the imperative or "tu dois", "il doit" at Readable.

decisions.choice: Narrative in the plain written style with the honorific for God: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 ... 말씀하셨다"; God speaks to Moses in 해라체 with 나 and 너
alternatives: 해요체 or 합쇼체 for God's speech
decisions.reason: As the Korean style guide (section 7a) and the Genesis and Pentateuch term sheets: the story is told in the plain style, God takes -시- and 께서, and God speaks in the plain style. The divine name is the span {{divine_name:주|야훼}} with the particle outside it; Korean has no deity_pronoun spans, since the honorific carries the respect the capital letter carries in English. Recorded once for Exodus 31-37.

decisions.choice: "phán" for the LORD speaking
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese style guide keeps "phán" for God speaking and "nói" for every human speaker; it is used through these chapters.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
decisions.reason: Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalizes pronouns for God has nothing to change; the Amharic text of this chapter has no such spans.

decisions.choice: called by name: chosen personally for a task
decisions.reason: To call someone by name is to single out and appoint that person (Isaiah 43:1; 45:3-4). Bezalel does not volunteer; God chooses him for the building of the tabernacle.

decisions.choice: son of Uri, son of Hur: Bezalel's father and grandfather, of Judah
decisions.reason: The family line is given in 1 Chronicles 2:18-20, where Hur is Bezalel's grandfather in the tribe of Judah. This Hur may be the one who held up Moses' hands (17:10-12) and was left in charge with Aaron (24:14), but the text does not say so.

decisions.choice: chosen ... by name
decisions.reason: Balanced says "chosen", the sense of the idiom (m1), and keeps "by name". Literal keeps "called by name".

decisions.choice: picked out ... for this work ... grandson
decisions.reason: Readable says what the calling is for, the work described in chapters 25-30, and calls Bezalel the grandson of Hur, as the family line shows (m2).

decisions.choice: "Betsaleel", "Ouri", "Hour"
decisions.reason: French uses the established French forms of the names, with "ts" for the Hebrew tsade as elsewhere in this translation; "Hour" is the Hur of 17:10 and 24:14. The same forms are used in chapters 35-38.

decisions.choice: "유다 지파 훌의 손자요 우리의 아들인 브살렐": the line of descent placed before the name
alternatives: "브살렐, 우리의 아들, 훌의 아들" in Hebrew order
decisions.reason: Korean puts a describing phrase before the noun, so the Hebrew "Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah" comes before the name at Literal and Balanced. "Son of Hur" here names the grandfather (meaning decision m2), so Korean says "손자". Readable gives the family in a sentence of its own, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Bết-sa-lê-ên", "U-ri", "Hu-rơ"
decisions.reason: The Protestant forms, as the Pentateuch terms note and the Vietnamese 2 Chronicles 1:5 have them.

decisions.choice: God says "Ta" and calls Moses "ngươi" (Literal) and "con" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As the Genesis terms note sets for God speaking to a person; "con" suits the closeness the book describes between God and Moses (33:11). Kept through chapters 31-37.

decisions.choice: Bezalel, filho de Uri, filho de Hur
decisions.reason: For the whole book (31:2; 35:30; 36:1-2; 37:1; 38:22): the craftsman's name keeps its usual Brazilian form "Bezalel", and his father and grandfather "Uri" and "Hur", forms Portuguese can write as the Hebrew sounds; Hur should match the Hur of 17:10 and 24:14. God speaks to Moses with "tu" ("Vê", "Presta atenção", "Olha").

decisions.choice: "ባስልኤል", "ኡሪ", "ሆር"; "እይ" (L), "ልብ በል" (B), "ተመልከት" (R)
decisions.reason: The names take their usual Ethiopian forms, as in Exodus 35-38. "See" is an imperative, not the particle "behold", so it is "እይ" at Literal rather than "እነሆ".

decisions.choice: "हूर के पुत्र ऊरी के पुत्र" (L); "ऊरी का पुत्र और हूर का पोता" (B, R)
alternatives: "ऊरी का पुत्र और हूर का पोता" at every level
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew chain "son of ... son of", as in 35:30 and 38:22; Balanced and Readable say "son" and "grandson", which is what the line means (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "Веселеил, сын Ура, сына Ора"; "колено" (L, B), "племя" (R)
decisions.reason: Names follow the traditional Russian Bible forms, as the Pentateuch note asks (Веселеил, Ур, Ор, Аголиав, Ахисамах); "колено" and "племя" for the tribe are the note's terms.

decisions.choice: Bezalel "ベツァルエル", Uri "ウリ", Hur "フル" (as in 24:14)
decisions.reason: Standard modern Japanese transcriptions of the Hebrew; first use of Bezalel and Uri in the book.

decisions.choice: re'eh: "見なさい" (L, R), "よく見なさい" (B)
decisions.reason: The style guide's form for a call to attention in speech (section 7a), not "見よ".

decisions.choice: Бецалел, Урі; Оголіав, Ахісамах (31:6)
decisions.reason: The craftsmen's names are transcribed from the Hebrew with г for h.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of God: God's own Spirit at work in a person
decisions.reason: The word means breath, wind or spirit. With "God" it is God's own Spirit, the same phrase as in Genesis 1:2, where the Spirit hovers over the waters before the world is given its form. Here the Spirit gives a craftsman the skill to make the place where God will dwell. The phrase could be taken as "a divine spirit", a gift of unusual ability, but elsewhere it is God's Spirit coming on a person (Numbers 24:2; 1 Samuel 10:10). Compare 28:3 and 35:31.

decisions.choice: wisdom, understanding, knowledge, workmanship: practical skill in a craft
decisions.reason: "Wisdom" here is practical skill, the know-how of a master craftsman (28:3; 35:35). With "understanding" and "knowledge" it describes the ability to plan the work and carry it out. The last word means work or craft of every kind. The same three gifts are said of God when he made the world (Proverbs 3:19-20).

decisions.choice: the Spirit of God, with a capital S
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no capital letters. "Spirit" is capitalized because the spirit is God's own (m1), as at Genesis 1:2 in this translation. The Spirit is never "it".

decisions.choice: so that he has (Balanced); I have given him (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the list joined by "with". Balanced and Readable say how the gifts follow from the filling with the Spirit.

decisions.choice: "Roho wa Mungu"
decisions.reason: With personal agreement ("wa"), "Roho wa Mungu" is God's own Spirit, as the English capital S shows (m1); "roho ya Mungu" would read as a breath or a spirit belonging to God. The same form is used at Genesis 1:2 and in the New Testament.

decisions.choice: "지혜와 총명과 지식" (L, B); "지혜와 이해력과 지식" (R)
decisions.reason: The three words name practical skill (meaning decision m2), but they are the words used of wisdom elsewhere; Korean keeps the familiar trio so the link can be seen, and the sentence around them ("온갖 일에", "만드는 데 필요한") shows that craft is meant. Readable uses the plainer "이해력" for understanding.

decisions.choice: "Thần Linh của Đức Chúa Trời"
decisions.reason: The form the Genesis terms note sets for "the Spirit of God" (Genesis 1:2), with capitals, as the English has a capital S.

decisions.choice: o Espírito de Deus; sabedoria, entendimento, conhecimento
decisions.reason: "Espírito" takes a capital, as the English "Spirit" does, because the spirit is God's own (m1), as at Genesis 1:2 in Portuguese. The three gifts are practical skill (m2); Portuguese keeps the three nouns, which can all mean know-how in a craft.

decisions.choice: "የእግዚአብሔር መንፈስ"
decisions.reason: Elohim here is plainly the one God and YHWH does not stand beside it, so it is "እግዚአብሔር", as the Pentateuch terms list directs; Readable "God" in verse 18 likewise.

decisions.choice: "Дух Божий" with a capital
decisions.reason: As in the English, "Дух" is capitalised because the spirit is God's own (m1), as the New Testament writes it in this translation.

decisions.choice: ruach elohim: "神の霊" at every level
decisions.reason: As at Genesis 1:2; Japanese has no capital letter, so the English "Spirit" is carried by the word itself.

records.literal_gloss: to design designs, to work in gold and in silver and in bronze,

en.L: to devise designs, to work in gold and in silver and in bronze,
en.B: to think out artistic designs and to carry them out in gold, silver and bronze,
en.R: He can plan beautiful designs and make them from gold, silver and bronze.

es.L: para idear diseños, para trabajar en oro y en plata y en bronce,
es.B: para concebir diseños artísticos y ejecutarlos en oro, plata y bronce,
es.R: Sabe trazar diseños hermosos y hacerlos en oro, plata y bronce.

fr.L: pour concevoir des plans, pour travailler dans l’or et dans l’argent et dans le bronze,
fr.B: pour imaginer des œuvres d’art et les réaliser en or, en argent et en bronze,
fr.R: Il sait dessiner de beaux motifs et les fabriquer en or, en argent et en bronze.

sw.L: ili kubuni michoro ya ustadi, kufanya kazi katika dhahabu na katika fedha na katika shaba,
sw.B: ili kubuni kazi za usanii na kuzitengeneza kwa dhahabu, fedha na shaba,
sw.R: Anaweza kubuni michoro mizuri na kuitengeneza kwa dhahabu, fedha na shaba.

vi.L: để nghĩ ra các mẫu [mỹ thuật], để làm [đồ] bằng vàng, bằng bạc và bằng đồng,
vi.B: để nghĩ ra các mẫu mỹ thuật và thực hiện chúng bằng vàng, bạc và đồng,
vi.R: Người có thể vẽ ra những mẫu đẹp và làm ra chúng bằng vàng, bạc và đồng.

ko.L: 도안들을 고안하고, 금과 은과 놋으로 일하며,
ko.B: 예술적인 도안을 생각해 내고 그것을 금과 은과 놋으로 만들어 내며,
ko.R: 그는 아름다운 무늬를 구상하고, 그것을 금과 은과 놋으로 만들 수 있다.

pt.L: para conceber desenhos, para trabalhar em ouro, e em prata, e em bronze,
pt.B: para criar desenhos artísticos e executá-los em ouro, prata e bronze,
pt.R: Ele sabe planejar desenhos bonitos e fazê-los em ouro, prata e bronze.

am.L: ንድፍ ለመንደፍ፣ በወርቅና በብር በነሐስም ለመሥራት፣
am.B: የጥበብ ንድፎችን እንዲያወጣና በወርቅ፣ በብርና በነሐስ እንዲሠራቸው፣
am.R: ያማሩ ንድፎችን ማውጣትና ከወርቅ፣ ከብርና ከነሐስ መሥራት ይችላል።

hi.L: कि कलात्मक नमूने सोचे, सोने और चाँदी और पीतल में काम करे,
hi.B: कि वह कलात्मक नमूने सोचे और उन्हें सोने, चाँदी और पीतल में बनाए,
hi.R: वह सुंदर नमूने सोच सकता है और उन्हें सोने, चाँदी और पीतल से बना सकता है।

ru.L: чтобы замышлять замыслы, работать с золотом, и серебром, и медью,
ru.B: чтобы придумывать художественные замыслы и исполнять их из золота, серебра и меди,
ru.R: Он может придумывать красивые узоры и делать их из золота, серебра и меди.

ja.L: 意匠を考案し、金と銀と青銅で作り、
ja.B: 芸術的な意匠を考え出し、それを金、銀、青銅で作り上げ、
ja.R: 彼は美しいデザインを考えて、それを金や銀や青銅で作ることができる。

uk.L: щоб задумувати задуми, щоб працювати в золоті, і в сріблі, і в міді,
uk.B: щоб обмірковувати мистецькі задуми й втілювати їх у золоті, сріблі й міді,
uk.R: Він уміє задумувати гарні візерунки й виготовляти їх із золота, срібла й міді.

decisions.choice: to devise designs: to plan artistic work
decisions.reason: The verb and the noun come from the same root, which means to think out or plan. It is used of the skilled weaver's work in 26:1 and 28:6. Bezalel is to plan the work as well as do it.

decisions.choice: He can ... beautiful
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence with Bezalel as its subject, and "beautiful" brings out that the designs are artistic.

decisions.choice: "놋" for bronze
decisions.reason: The metal is copper or bronze; "놋" is the word used for the bronze altar and basin through Exodus and Kings, so the tabernacle's metals keep one name. Recorded once for these chapters.

source.text: וּבַחֲרֹ֥שֶׁת אֶ֛בֶן לְמַלֹּ֖את וּבַחֲרֹ֣שֶׁת עֵ֑ץ לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת בְּכָל־מְלָאכָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and in cutting of stone for setting, and in carving of wood, to work in all workmanship.

en.L: and in cutting of stone for setting, and in carving of wood, to work in every [kind of] workmanship.
en.B: to cut stones for mounting, to carve wood, and to do every kind of skilled work.
en.R: He can shape gemstones for mounting, carve wood, and do every other kind of craft work.

es.L: y en el tallado de piedras para engastar, y en la talla de madera, para trabajar en toda [clase de] obra.
es.B: para tallar piedras de engaste, labrar la madera y realizar toda clase de trabajos artísticos.
es.R: Sabe tallar piedras preciosas para montarlas, labrar madera y hacer cualquier otro trabajo artesanal.

fr.L: et dans la taille des pierres à sertir, et dans la sculpture du bois, pour exécuter toute [sorte d’]ouvrage.
fr.B: pour tailler des pierres à sertir, sculpter le bois et faire toutes sortes de travaux d’art.
fr.R: Il sait tailler des pierres précieuses pour les monter, sculpter le bois et faire toutes sortes d’autres travaux d’artisan.

sw.L: na katika kuchonga vito vya kupachikwa, na katika kuchonga mbao, ili kufanya kila [aina ya] kazi.
sw.B: kuchonga vito vya kupachikwa, kuchonga mbao, na kufanya kila aina ya kazi ya ustadi.
sw.R: Anaweza kuchonga vito vya thamani ili vipachikwe, kuchonga mbao, na kufanya kila aina nyingine ya kazi ya ufundi.

vi.L: và trong việc cắt đá để gắn [vào khung], và trong việc chạm gỗ, để làm mọi [loại] công việc.
vi.B: để cắt đá quý để gắn vào khung, để chạm gỗ, và để làm mọi loại công việc khéo léo.
vi.R: Người có thể mài giũa đá quý để gắn vào khung, chạm trổ gỗ, và làm mọi thứ việc thủ công khác.

ko.L: 또 박을 돌을 깎고 나무를 새겨서 모든 [종류의] 솜씨를 부리게 하였다.
ko.B: 보석을 깎아 물리고 나무를 조각하는 일까지, 모든 정교한 일을 할 수 있게 했다.
ko.R: 그는 보석을 다듬어 박을 수 있고, 나무를 조각할 수 있으며, 그 밖의 온갖 공예 일을 할 수 있다.

pt.L: e em lapidação de pedras para engaste, e em entalhe de madeira, para trabalhar em toda [espécie de] obra.
pt.B: para lapidar pedras e engastá-las, para entalhar madeira e para fazer todo tipo de trabalho artístico.
pt.R: Ele sabe lapidar pedras preciosas para serem engastadas, entalhar madeira e fazer qualquer outro tipo de trabalho artesanal.

am.L: ለፈርጥ የሚሆን ድንጋይ በመቅረጽ፣ እንጨትም በመጥረብ፣ በሙያ ሁሉ ለመሥራት።
am.B: ለፈርጥ የሚሆኑ ድንጋዮችን እንዲቀርጽ፣ እንጨት እንዲጠርብና ማንኛውንም የጥበብ ሥራ እንዲሠራ።
am.R: ለፈርጥ የሚሆኑ የከበሩ ድንጋዮችን መቅረጽ፣ እንጨት መጥረብና ሌላውንም የእጅ ሥራ ሁሉ መሥራት ይችላል።

hi.L: और जड़ने के लिए पत्थर काटने में, और लकड़ी पर नक़्क़ाशी करने में, कि हर [प्रकार की] कारीगरी में काम करे।
hi.B: जड़ने के लिए पत्थर काटे, लकड़ी पर नक़्क़ाशी करे, और हर प्रकार का कुशल काम करे।
hi.R: वह जड़ने के लिए क़ीमती पत्थरों को तराश सकता है, लकड़ी पर नक़्क़ाशी कर सकता है, और हर दूसरी तरह की कारीगरी कर सकता है।

ru.L: и в резьбе камней для вставки, и в резьбе по дереву, чтобы работать во всяком мастерстве.
ru.B: гранить камни для оправ, резать по дереву и выполнять всякую искусную работу.
ru.R: Он может гранить драгоценные камни для оправ, резать по дереву и делать любую другую работу мастера.

ja.L: はめ込むための石を刻み、木を彫り、あらゆる技の仕事をするためである。
ja.B: はめ込む宝石を刻み、木を彫り、あらゆる熟練した仕事をするためである。
ja.R: また、宝石をみがいてはめ込むことも、木を彫ることも、そのほかどんな細工の仕事もできる。

uk.L: і в обробці каменю для оправи, і в різьбленні дерева, щоб робити всяку роботу.
uk.B: обробляти камені для оправи, різьбити по дереву й робити всяку майстерну роботу.
uk.R: Він уміє обробляти дорогоцінні камені для оправи, різьбити по дереву й робити будь-яку іншу ремісничу роботу.

decisions.choice: cutting of stone for setting: shaping precious stones to be mounted
decisions.reason: "For filling" means stones set into mountings, as in the breastpiece, where the twelve stones are set in gold (28:17-20) and the two onyx stones on the ephod (28:9-11).

decisions.choice: gemstones
decisions.reason: The stones to be set are precious stones (m1), so Readable says "gemstones".

source.text: וַאֲנִ֞י הִנֵּ֧ה נָתַ֣תִּי אִתּ֗וֹ אֵ֣ת אָהֳלִיאָ֞ב בֶּן־אֲחִֽיסָמָךְ֙ לְמַטֵּה־דָ֔ן וּבְלֵ֥ב כָּל־חֲכַם־לֵ֖ב נָתַ֣תִּי חָכְמָ֑ה וְעָשׂ֕וּ אֵ֖ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתִֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I, here, I have given with him Oholiab son of Ahisamach of [the] tribe of Dan; and in [the] heart of every wise of heart I have put wisdom, and they will make all that I have commanded you:

en.L: And I, see, I have appointed with him Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan; and in the heart of every [one] wise of heart I have put wisdom, and they will make all that I have commanded you:
en.B: I myself have also named Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, to be his partner. Into the hearts of all who are wise of heart I have put wisdom, so that they will make all that I have commanded you:
en.R: I have also chosen Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, to work alongside him. And every worker who has a gift for this work has received more wisdom from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Together they will make everything I have commanded you.

es.L: Y yo, he aquí, he designado con él a Oholiab hijo de Ahisamac, de la tribu de Dan; y en el corazón de todo sabio de corazón he puesto sabiduría, y harán todo lo que te he mandado:
es.B: Yo mismo he nombrado también a Oholiab hijo de Ahisamac, de la tribu de Dan, para que sea su compañero. En el corazón de todos los sabios de corazón he puesto sabiduría, para que hagan todo lo que te he mandado:
es.R: También he elegido a Oholiab hijo de Ahisamac, de la tribu de Dan, para que trabaje junto a él. Y todo trabajador que tiene un don para esta obra ha recibido de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} más sabiduría. Juntos harán todo lo que te he mandado.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, voici, j’ai désigné avec lui Oholiab, fils d’Ahisamak, de la tribu de Dan ; et dans le cœur de chaque [personne] sage de cœur j’ai mis la sagesse, et ils feront tout ce que je t’ai ordonné :
fr.B: Moi-même, j’ai aussi désigné Oholiab, fils d’Ahisamak, de la tribu de Dan, pour être son associé. Dans le cœur de tous ceux qui sont sages de cœur, j’ai mis la sagesse, afin qu’ils fassent tout ce que je t’ai ordonné :
fr.R: J’ai aussi choisi Oholiab, fils d’Ahisamak, de la tribu de Dan, pour travailler à ses côtés. Et tous les ouvriers qui ont un don pour ce travail ont reçu de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} plus de sagesse. Ensemble, ils feront tout ce que je t’ai ordonné.

sw.L: Nami, tazama, nimemweka pamoja naye Oholiabu mwana wa Ahisamaki, wa kabila la Dani; na katika moyo wa kila mwenye moyo wa hekima nimetia hekima, nao watafanya yote niliyokuamuru:
sw.B: Mimi mwenyewe nimemteua pia Oholiabu mwana wa Ahisamaki, wa kabila la Dani, awe msaidizi wake. Mioyoni mwa wote wenye moyo wa hekima nimetia hekima, ili watengeneze yote niliyokuamuru:
sw.R: Pia nimemchagua Oholiabu mwana wa Ahisamaki, wa kabila la Dani, afanye kazi pamoja naye. Na kila fundi mwenye kipawa cha kazi hii amepokea hekima zaidi kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}. Kwa pamoja watatengeneza kila kitu nilichokuamuru.

vi.L: Còn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã chỉ định cùng với người Ô-hô-li-áp con trai A-hi-sa-mạc, thuộc chi tộc Đan; và trong lòng mọi người có lòng khôn ngoan, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đặt sự khôn ngoan, để họ làm mọi điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã truyền cho ngươi:
vi.B: Chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng đã chỉ định Ô-hô-li-áp con trai A-hi-sa-mạc, thuộc chi tộc Đan, làm người cộng tác với người. Ta đã đặt sự khôn ngoan vào lòng mọi người thợ khéo, để họ làm mọi điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã truyền cho con:
vi.R: Ta cũng đã chọn Ô-hô-li-áp con trai A-hi-sa-mạc, thuộc chi tộc Đan, để làm việc cùng với người. Mọi người thợ có tài trong công việc này cũng đã nhận thêm sự khôn ngoan từ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Họ sẽ cùng nhau làm mọi thứ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã truyền cho con.

ko.L: 그리고 나, 보아라, 내가 단 지파 아히사막의 아들 오홀리압을 그와 함께 세웠고, 마음이 지혜로운 모든 [사람의] 마음에 내가 지혜를 넣었으니, 그들이 내가 너에게 명령한 모든 것을 만들 것이다.
ko.B: 또 내가 친히 단 지파 아히사막의 아들 오홀리압을 그의 동역자로 정해 주었다. 그리고 마음이 지혜로운 모든 사람의 마음에 지혜를 넣어 주었으니, 그들이 내가 너에게 명령한 모든 것을 만들 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 또 단 지파 사람 아히사막의 아들 오홀리압을 골라서 그와 함께 일하게 했다. 이 일에 재능이 있는 일꾼들에게도 내가 지혜를 더 주었다. 그들이 함께 내가 너에게 명령한 것을 모두 만들 것이다.

pt.L: E eu, eis que dei com ele Aoliabe, filho de Aisamaque, da tribo de Dã; e no coração de todo sábio de coração pus sabedoria, e farão tudo o que te ordenei:
pt.B: Eu mesmo designei também Aoliabe, filho de Aisamaque, da tribo de Dã, para ser seu companheiro. E no coração de todos os que são hábeis eu pus sabedoria, para que façam tudo o que te ordenei:
pt.R: Também escolhi Aoliabe, filho de Aisamaque, da tribo de Dã, para trabalhar ao lado de Bezalel. E todo artesão que tem talento para esse trabalho recebeu de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} ainda mais sabedoria. Juntos eles vão fazer tudo o que eu te ordenei.

am.L: እኔም፣ እይ፣ ከዳን ነገድ የሆነውን የአሂሳማክን ልጅ ኦሆሊያብን ከእርሱ ጋር ሰጥቻለሁ፤ በልበ ጥበበኞች ሁሉ ልብ ውስጥም ጥበብን አኑሬአለሁ፤ ያዘዝኩህንም ሁሉ ይሠራሉ፦
am.B: እኔ ራሴም ከዳን ነገድ የሆነውን የአሂሳማክን ልጅ ኦሆሊያብን ረዳቱ እንዲሆን መድቤዋለሁ። ጥበበኛ ልብ ባላቸው ሁሉ ልብ ውስጥ ጥበብን አኑሬአለሁ፤ ይኸውም ያዘዝኩህን ሁሉ እንዲሠሩ ነው፦
am.R: ከዳን ነገድ የሆነውን የአሂሳማክን ልጅ ኦሆሊያብንም ከእርሱ ጋር እንዲሠራ መርጬዋለሁ። ለዚህ ሥራ ችሎታ ያለው ሠራተኛ ሁሉ ከእኔ ተጨማሪ ጥበብ ተቀብሏል። አንድ ላይ ሆነው ያዘዝኩህን ሁሉ ይሠራሉ።

hi.L: और मैं, देखो, मैंने उसके साथ दान के गोत्र के अहीसामाक के पुत्र ओहोलीआब को ठहराया है; और हर एक मन के बुद्धिमान के मन में मैंने बुद्धि डाली है, और वे वह सब बनाएँगे जिसकी मैंने तुम्हें आज्ञा दी है:
hi.B: मैंने स्वयं दान के गोत्र के अहीसामाक के पुत्र ओहोलीआब को भी उसका साथी ठहराया है। सब कुशल लोगों के मन में मैंने बुद्धि डाली है, ताकि वे वह सब बनाएँ जिसकी मैंने तुम्हें आज्ञा दी है:
hi.R: मैंने दान के गोत्र के अहीसामाक के पुत्र ओहोलीआब को भी उसके साथ काम करने के लिए चुना है। और जिस-जिस कारीगर में इस काम का गुण है, उसे मैंने और बुद्धि दी है। वे मिलकर वह सब बनाएँगे जिसकी मैंने तुम्हें आज्ञा दी है।

ru.L: И {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}}, вот, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} дал с ним Аголиава, сына Ахисамаха, из колена Дана; и в сердце всякого мудрого сердцем {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} вложил мудрость, и сделают они всё, что {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} повелел тебе:
ru.B: Я и сам назначил ему в помощники Аголиава, сына Ахисамаха, из колена Дана. В сердца всех мудрых сердцем {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} вложил мудрость, чтобы они сделали всё, что {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} повелел тебе:
ru.R: Я также выбрал Аголиава, сына Ахисамаха, из племени Дана, чтобы он работал вместе с ним. И каждый мастер, у которого есть дар для этой работы, получил от {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} ещё больше мудрости. Вместе они сделают всё, что {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} тебе повелел.

ja.L: そしてわたしは、見なさい、ダン部族のアヒサマクの子オホリアブを彼と共に与えた。そして心に知恵のあるすべての者の心に、わたしは知恵を授けた。彼らは、わたしがあなたに命じたすべてのものを作る。
ja.B: わたし自身も、ダン族のアヒサマクの子オホリアブを、彼の協力者として任命した。また、心に知恵のある者すべての心に知恵を授けた。彼らが作るのは、わたしがあなたに命じた次のすべてのものである。
ja.R: わたしはまた、ダンの部族のアヒサマクの息子オホリアブを選び、ベツァルエルと一緒に働かせる。この仕事の才能のある職人たちにも、わたしはさらに知恵を与えた。彼らは力を合わせて、わたしがあなたに命じたものを全部作る。

uk.L: А Я, ось Я дав з ним Оголіава, сина Ахісамаха, з племені Дана; і в серце кожного мудрого серцем Я вклав мудрість, і зроблять вони все, що Я наказав тобі:
uk.B: Я й сам призначив йому в помічники Оголіава, сина Ахісамаха, з племені Дана. У серця всіх, хто мудрий серцем, Я вклав мудрість, щоб вони зробили все, що Я тобі наказав:
uk.R: Я вибрав також Оголіава, сина Ахісамаха, з племені Дана, щоб він працював поруч з ним. І кожен майстер, що має хист до цієї праці, отримав від {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}} ще більше мудрості. Разом вони зроблять усе, що Я тобі звелів.

decisions.choice: Oholiab of the tribe of Dan: a second master craftsman
decisions.reason: Oholiab is Bezalel's helper. In 38:23 he is an engraver, a designer and an embroiderer in blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen. Judah was one of the leading tribes and Dan one of the least; workers from both build the tabernacle.

decisions.choice: every wise of heart: everyone with skill, to whom God gives more skill
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of the mind and will. Someone "wise of heart" is a skilled worker (28:3; 35:10, 25). God puts wisdom into those who already have it: the gift is his as well as theirs.

decisions.choice: named ... to be his partner
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "I have given with him", meaning appointed to work beside him. Literal says "appointed with him".

decisions.choice: every worker who has a gift for this work has received more wisdom from me
decisions.reason: Readable explains "wise of heart" as having a gift for the work and makes clear that God adds to the skill they have (m2).

decisions.choice: "마음이 지혜로운" for "wise of heart"
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew picture of the heart as the seat of skill, which Korean can bear; the meaning decision says it means a skilled person, and Readable says "재능이 있는 일꾼들". Used the same way in chapters 35-36.

decisions.choice: "Ô-hô-li-áp", "A-hi-sa-mạc"
decisions.reason: Ô-hô-li-áp is the form of the Pentateuch terms note; A-hi-sa-mạc follows the usual Protestant form.

decisions.choice: Aoliabe, filho de Aisamaque, da tribo de Dã
decisions.reason: For the whole book (31:6; 35:34; 36:1-2; 38:23): "Aoliabe" is the usual Brazilian form of Oholiab, with the final -e Portuguese gives a name ending in b, and his father's name is "Aisamaque", with "qu" for the k-sound and a final -e. "Dã" is the tribe's name (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md). "Sábio de coração" (L) and "hábeis" (B) follow 28:3. Readable names Bezalel for "him".

decisions.choice: "ኦሆሊያብ", "የአሂሳማክ ልጅ"
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 38:23: "ኤልያብ" is avoided because it is another name (Eliab).

decisions.choice: Oholiab "オホリアブ", Ahisamach "アヒサマク"
decisions.reason: Standard modern Japanese transcriptions of the Hebrew; first use in the book.

decisions.choice: wise of heart: "心に知恵のある者" (L, B), "才能のある職人" (R)
decisions.reason: As at 28:3; skill in a craft (m2).

ko.B: 곧 회막과 증거궤와 그 위에 덮는 속죄소와 회막의 다른 모든 기구,
ko.R: 그들은 회막을 만들고, 언약을 새긴 돌판을 넣어 두는 궤를 만들고, 궤의 뚜껑을 만들 것이다. 이 뚜껑은 죄를 덮어 주는 자리이다. 회막에 쓸 다른 모든 물건도 만들 것이다.

am.L: የመገናኛውን ድንኳን፣ የምስክሩንም ታቦት፣ በላዩ ያለውንም የስርየት መክደኛ፣ የድንኳኑንም ዕቃዎች ሁሉ፣
am.B: የመገናኛውን ድንኳን፣ የምስክሩን ታቦትና በላዩ ያለውን የስርየት መክደኛ፣ የድንኳኑንም ሌሎች ዕቃዎች ሁሉ፤
am.R: የመገናኛውን ድንኳን፣ የቃል ኪዳኑ ጽላቶች የሚቀመጡበትን ታቦትና የታቦቱን መክደኛ ይሠራሉ፤ ይህ መክደኛ ኃጢአት የሚሰረይበት ስፍራ ነው። ለድንኳኑ የሚያስፈልጉትን ሌሎች ነገሮች ሁሉ ይሠራሉ፤

ru.L: шатёр встречи, и ковчег свидетельства, и место умилостивления, которое на нём, и все принадлежности шатра,

ja.B: 会見の天幕、上に贖いの座を載せた証しの箱、天幕のほかのすべての器具、
ja.R: 彼らは、神と会うテントと、契約の板を納めた箱と、箱のふたである贖いの座を作る。贖いの座は、罪がおおわれる所である。また、テントのためのほかの物もすべて作る。

decisions.choice: the ark of the testimony: the chest that holds the tablets of the covenant
decisions.reason: "The testimony" is the two tablets of stone on which the covenant was written, placed in the ark (25:16, 21; verse 18). They bear witness to the covenant between God and Israel.

decisions.choice: the mercy seat: the lid of the ark, the place where sin is covered
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb used for making atonement. It names the gold lid of the ark, where God would meet with Moses (25:17-22) and where the blood was sprinkled on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:14-15).

decisions.choice: the ark that holds the covenant tablets ... the lid of the ark, the place where sins are covered
decisions.reason: Readable says what the ark and its lid are (m1, m2). Literal and Balanced keep "ark of the testimony" and "mercy seat". Readable also repeats "They will make" to start the list as new sentences.

decisions.choice: "회막", "증거궤", "속죄소" (L, B); explained at R
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch term sheet: the tent of meeting is "회막", the ark of the testimony "증거궤", the atonement cover "속죄소". Readable explains the ark and the cover as the English Readable does ("the place where sins are covered"). Recorded once for these chapters.

decisions.choice: "Lều Hội Kiến", "hòm chứng ước", "nắp thi ân"
decisions.reason: The words the Pentateuch terms note sets for the tent of meeting, the ark of the testimony and the atonement cover. Readable explains the ark and the cover, as the English does.

decisions.choice: the anointing oil and the fragrant incense: made by the recipes of 30:22-38
decisions.reason: The oil was used to anoint the tent, its furnishings and the priests, and the incense was burned on the gold altar each morning and evening (30:7-8). Both were holy and could not be copied for ordinary use (30:32-33, 37-38).

decisions.choice: for the holy place: for the sanctuary
decisions.reason: "The holy" here means the sanctuary as a whole, where the incense was burned and the oil was used.

decisions.choice: according to all that I have commanded: the work must follow God's pattern exactly
decisions.reason: The tabernacle is built to the pattern God showed Moses (25:9, 40). The account of the building repeats that it was done "as the LORD commanded Moses" (39:42-43).

decisions.choice: special
decisions.reason: The anointing oil was set apart for holy use (30:32); Readable says "special" to show it is not ordinary oil.

decisions.choice: "기름 부음에 쓰는 기름" (L); "기름 부을 때 쓰는 기름" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Sino-Korean "관유" is a church term few readers know; Korean describes the oil by its use.

decisions.choice: Yahweh said to Moses: the last of the speeches on the mountain, about the Sabbath
decisions.reason: The instructions that begin in 25:1 are divided by the words "Yahweh spoke (or said) to Moses" at 30:11, 17, 22, 34; 31:1 and here, seven speeches in all. The last of them is about the Sabbath, the seventh day, as the account of creation ends with the seventh day (Genesis 2:1-3).

records.literal_gloss: And you, speak to [the] sons of Israel, saying, surely my sabbaths you shall keep, for a sign it [is] between me and between you throughout your generations, to know that I [am] Yahweh who sets you apart.

en.L: "And you, speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, saying, 'Surely {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths you shall keep, for it [is] a sign between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and you throughout your generations, that [you may] know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who sanctifies you.
en.B: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'Whatever else you do, keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths. The Sabbath is a sign between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and you for all your generations, so that you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the one who sets you apart as holy.
en.R: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'No matter what, keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbath days. They are a sign between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and you for all time to come. They show that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who has made you {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own holy people.

Muestran que yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que {{plural_you:los|os}} ha hecho {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} propio pueblo santo.

fr.R: « Dis aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} : “Quoi qu’il arrive, respectez {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} jours de sabbat. vi.L: "Còn ngươi, hãy nói với con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên rằng: 'Chắc chắn các ngươi phải giữ các ngày Sa-bát của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, vì đó [là] dấu hiệu giữa {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và các ngươi qua các thế hệ của các ngươi, để [các ngươi] biết rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} [là] {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đấng thánh hóa các ngươi.

vi.R: "Hãy nói với dân Y-sơ-ra-ên: 'Dù thế nào đi nữa, các ngươi phải giữ các ngày Sa-bát của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Các ngày ấy là dấu hiệu giữa {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và các ngươi đời đời. ko.L: "그리고 너는 이스라엘 자손에게 말하여 일러라. '반드시 너희는 내 안식일들을 지켜라. 그것은 너희 대대로 나와 너희 사이의 표징이니, 나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 너희를 거룩하게 하는 이임을 [너희가] 알게 하려는 것이다.

ko.R: "너는 이스라엘 사람들에게 이렇게 말하여라. '무슨 일이 있어도 너희는 내 안식일을 지켜야 한다. 안식일은 너희가 대대로 나와 맺은 관계를 보여 주는 표징이다. 그것은 나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 너희를 거룩한 내 백성으로 삼았다는 것을 보여 준다.

pt.L: "E tu, fala aos filhos de Israel, dizendo: 'Certamente vocês guardarão os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} sábados, porque [é] um sinal entre {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} e vocês pelas suas gerações, para que saibam que eu [sou] {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, que os santifica.

pt.R: "Diz aos israelitas: 'Aconteça o que acontecer, guardem os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} sábados. Eles são um sinal entre {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} e vocês, em todas as gerações que vierem. Eles mostram que eu sou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, que fez de vocês o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo santo.

am.L: «አንተም ለእስራኤል ልጆች እንዲህ ብለህ ተናገር፦ “በእውነት ሰንበቶቼን ጠብቁ፤ የምቀድሳችሁ እኔ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንደ ሆንኩ ታውቁ ዘንድ በትውልዳችሁ ሁሉ በእኔና በእናንተ መካከል ምልክት ነውና።

decisions.choice: surely: above all, or nevertheless
decisions.reason: The word stresses what follows. After the instructions for the tabernacle it may mean "above all", or "nevertheless": even the holy work of building the sanctuary must stop on the Sabbath. Chapter 35 begins the building with the Sabbath command for the same reason (35:2-3).

decisions.choice: my Sabbaths ... a sign between me and you: the Sabbath marks the covenant
decisions.reason: The Sabbaths are God's, and keeping them is a sign that Israel belongs to him, as the rainbow (Genesis 9:12-17) and circumcision (Genesis 17:11) are signs of covenants. The plural means each weekly Sabbath (verses 14-15; compare Leviticus 19:3, 30; Ezekiel 20:12).

decisions.choice: who sanctifies you: who makes you holy, setting you apart as his own
decisions.reason: The verb means to make or declare holy. God set the seventh day apart as holy (Genesis 2:3; 20:11); the people who keep it are set apart as his (19:6; Leviticus 20:8).

decisions.choice: Whatever else you do (Balanced); No matter what (Readable)
decisions.reason: These bring out the stress of "surely" (m1). Literal keeps "surely".

decisions.choice: who has made you my own holy people
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what it means for God to make the people holy (m3).

decisions.choice: "un signe"
decisions.reason: The Sabbath as "un signe" between God and Israel, the same word as for the signs in Egypt and the sign of circumcision (Genesis 17:11), so that the link between them (m2) stays visible. Spanish "una señal" and Swahili "ishara" do the same. Used again in verse 17.

decisions.choice: "이스라엘 자손" (L); "이스라엘 백성" (B); "이스라엘 사람들" (R), with no gender span
alternatives: a gender setting span, as in the English
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch term sheet. The Korean words already include women and men, so the Korean has nothing for the gender setting to switch. Recorded once for these chapters.

decisions.choice: God's commands in 해라체: "지켜라" (L, B); "지켜야 한다" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch term sheet: God's commands use -하라 / -하지 말라 at Literal and Balanced, and -해야 한다 / -하면 안 된다 at Readable. Recorded once for these chapters.

decisions.choice: "con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên" (Literal); "dân Y-sơ-ra-ên" (Balanced, Readable), with no gender span
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch terms note sets. Both Vietnamese phrases already take in men and women, so the English gender setting has no counterpart.

decisions.choice: God speaks to Israel as "các ngươi", with "phải" for the command
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch terms note sets "ngươi" / "các ngươi" with "phải" and "không được" for God's commands; used through these chapters.

decisions.choice: vocês; guardarão (L), guardem (B, R); os sábados
decisions.reason: God's words for Israel here are plural, so the message Moses passes on says "vocês" (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md), with the future at Literal and the plural imperative at Balanced and Readable; God still speaks to Moses himself with "tu" ("fala", "Diz"). "Sábado" is lowercase, as the style guide sets. The "filhos de Israel" take no gender setting (1:7).

decisions.choice: "ሰንበቶቼን ጠብቁ"; "የምቀድሳችሁ" (L), "ቀድሼ የምለያችሁ" (B), "የራሴ ቅዱስ ሕዝብ ያደረግኋችሁ" (R)
decisions.reason: "Keep" is "መጠበቅ", the usual word for observing the Sabbath; "who sanctifies you" uses "መቀደስ" as in chapter 29, with Readable spelling out the sense as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "सब्त"; no deity_pronoun spans; "इस्राएली" with no gender span at B and R
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in the English
decisions.reason: "सब्त" is the Pentateuch note's word for the Sabbath. Devanagari has no capital letters, so this chapter has no deity_pronoun spans; Balanced and Readable say "इस्राएली", which already includes everyone, and only Literal has the gender span.

decisions.choice: "суббота"
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch note keeps "суббота" for the Sabbath, as the New Testament does; it is the living Russian word for the day.

decisions.choice: ak: "必ず" (L), "何をおいても" (B), "何があっても" (R)
decisions.reason: Above all, or nevertheless (m1, uncertain); the Balanced and Readable wordings follow the English's "Whatever else you do" / "No matter what".

records.literal_gloss: And you shall keep the sabbath, for a holy thing it [is] to you. Those who profane it surely shall be put to death; for whoever does on it work, and will be cut off that person from [the] midst of her people.

en.L: And you shall keep the Sabbath, for it [is] holy to you. Whoever profanes it shall surely be put to death; for whoever does work on it, that person shall be cut off from the midst of {{gender:their|his}} people.
en.B: So you are to keep the Sabbath, for it is a holy day for you. If anyone profanes it, that person must be put to death. If anyone works on it, that person will be cut off from among {{gender:their|his}} people.
en.R: Keep the Sabbath, because it is a holy day for you. Anyone who treats it like an ordinary day must be put to death. Anyone who works on that day must be removed from the people.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:guardarán|guardaréis}} el sábado, porque santo [es] para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. El que lo profane, sin falta se le dará muerte; porque cualquiera que haga en él trabajo, esa persona será cortada de en medio de su pueblo.
es.B: {{plural_you:Guardarán|Guardaréis}}, pues, el sábado, porque es para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} un día santo. Si alguien lo profana, será condenado a muerte. Si alguien trabaja en él, será cortado de en medio de su pueblo.
es.R: {{plural_you:Guarden|Guardad}} el sábado, porque es un día santo para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. El que lo trate como un día cualquiera debe ser condenado a muerte. El que trabaje ese día debe ser expulsado del pueblo.

fr.L: Et vous garderez le sabbat, car il [est] saint pour vous. Celui qui le profanera sera certainement mis à mort ; car quiconque fera en lui un travail, cette personne sera retranchée du milieu de son peuple.
fr.B: Vous garderez donc le sabbat, car c’est pour vous un jour saint. Si quelqu’un le profane, il sera mis à mort. Si quelqu’un y fait un travail, il sera retranché du milieu de son peuple.
fr.R: Respectez le sabbat, car c’est un jour saint pour vous. Celui qui le traite comme un jour ordinaire doit être mis à mort. Celui qui travaille ce jour-là doit être retiré du peuple.

sw.L: Nanyi mtaishika Sabato, kwa maana [ni] takatifu kwenu. Kila anayeitia unajisi kwa hakika atauawa; kwa maana kila aifanyaye kazi siku hiyo, mtu huyo atakatiliwa mbali kutoka katikati ya watu wake.
sw.B: Basi mtaishika Sabato, kwa sababu ni siku takatifu kwenu. Mtu yeyote akiitia unajisi, atauawa. Mtu yeyote akifanya kazi siku hiyo, atakatiliwa mbali kutoka kati ya watu wake.
sw.R: Shikeni Sabato, kwa sababu ni siku takatifu kwenu. Mtu yeyote anayeichukulia kama siku ya kawaida lazima auawe. Mtu yeyote anayefanya kazi siku hiyo lazima aondolewe kati ya watu.

vi.L: Vậy các ngươi phải giữ ngày Sa-bát, vì đó [là ngày] thánh cho các ngươi. Kẻ nào làm ô uế ngày ấy chắc chắn phải bị xử tử; vì ai làm việc trong ngày ấy, người đó sẽ bị khai trừ khỏi giữa dân mình.
vi.B: Vậy các ngươi phải giữ ngày Sa-bát, vì đó là ngày thánh cho các ngươi. Ai xúc phạm ngày ấy phải bị xử tử. Ai làm việc trong ngày ấy, người đó sẽ bị khai trừ khỏi dân mình.
vi.R: Hãy giữ ngày Sa-bát, vì đó là ngày thánh cho các ngươi. Ai coi ngày ấy như một ngày thường thì phải bị xử tử. Ai làm việc trong ngày ấy thì phải bị loại ra khỏi dân chúng.

ko.L: 그러므로 너희는 안식일을 지켜라. 그것은 너희에게 거룩하기 때문이다. 그것을 더럽히는 자는 반드시 죽임을 당할 것이다. 누구든지 그날에 일을 하면, 그 사람은 자기 백성 가운데서 끊어질 것이다.
ko.B: 그러므로 너희는 안식일을 지켜라. 안식일은 너희에게 거룩한 날이다. 누구든지 그날을 더럽히면 그 사람은 반드시 죽여야 한다. 누구든지 그날에 일을 하면 그 사람은 자기 백성 가운데서 끊어질 것이다.
ko.R: 안식일을 지켜야 한다. 그날은 너희에게 거룩한 날이다. 그날을 다른 날처럼 함부로 대하는 사람은 죽여야 한다. 그날에 일하는 사람은 백성 가운데서 끊어져야 한다.

pt.L: E guardarão o sábado, porque é santo para vocês. Quem o profanar certamente será morto; porque quem fizer nele algum trabalho, essa pessoa será cortada do meio do seu povo.
pt.B: Guardem, pois, o sábado, porque é um dia santo para vocês. Quem o profanar deverá ser morto. Quem trabalhar nesse dia será eliminado do meio do seu povo.
pt.R: Guardem o sábado, porque é um dia santo para vocês. Quem tratar esse dia como um dia comum tem de ser morto. Quem trabalhar nesse dia deve ser eliminado do povo.

ru.L: И соблюдайте субботу, потому что она святыня для вас. Оскверняющий её непременно будет предан смерти; потому что всякий, кто делает в неё работу, — истребится та душа из среды народа своего.
ru.B: Соблюдайте субботу, потому что это святой день для вас. Тот, кто осквернит её, должен быть предан смерти. Кто будет работать в этот день, тот будет истреблён из среды своего народа.
ru.R: Соблюдайте субботу, потому что это святой день для вас. Кто будет обращаться с ним, как с обычным днём, должен быть предан смерти. Кто будет работать в этот день, должен быть удалён из народа.

ja.L: そしてあなたがたは安息日を守りなさい。それはあなたがたにとって聖なるものだからである。それを汚す者は必ず死刑に処せられる。それに仕事をする者はだれでも、その者はその民のただ中から断たれるからである。
ja.B: だから、安息日を守りなさい。それはあなたがたにとって聖なる日である。これを汚す者は必ず死刑に処せられる。この日に仕事をする者はだれでも、自分の民の中から断たれる。
ja.R: 安息日を守りなさい。それは、あなたたちにとって聖なる日だからである。この日を普通の日のように扱う者は、死刑にされなければならない。この日に仕事をする者は、民の中から除かれなければならない。

uk.L: І зберігайте суботу, бо вона свята для вас. Хто осквернить її, неодмінно буде скараний на смерть; бо кожен, хто робитиме в неї роботу, — та душа буде відтята з-посеред свого народу.
uk.B: Тож зберігайте суботу, бо це святий день для вас. Якщо хтось осквернить її, його треба скарати на смерть. Якщо хтось працюватиме того дня, ця людина буде відтята від свого народу.
uk.R: Дотримуйтеся суботи, бо це святий день для вас. Кожного, хто вважатиме її звичайним днем, треба скарати на смерть. Кожного, хто працюватиме того дня, треба вилучити з народу.

decisions.choice: profanes: treats what is holy as common
decisions.reason: The verb is the opposite of making holy (verse 13). To profane the Sabbath is to use it like any other day, chiefly by working on it, as the next clause explains.

decisions.choice: surely shall be put to death: the death penalty, stated firmly
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled in Hebrew to make the sentence firm, as in the laws of 21:12-17. Numbers 15:32-36 tells of the sentence being carried out.

decisions.choice: cut off from among its people: removed from the people of God
decisions.reason: To be cut off is to lose one's place in Israel, by death or by being put out of the community. The verse does not say whether the people or God himself carries it out; Leviticus 20:2-6 speaks of both.

decisions.choice: treats it like an ordinary day ... removed from the people
decisions.reason: Readable says what profaning means (m1) and puts "cut off" in plain words (m3).

decisions.choice: "esa persona ... su pueblo", with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English needs {{gender:their|his}}. Spanish "su" does not mark gender, so the setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: "cette personne ... son peuple", "quelqu'un ... son peuple", with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English needs {{gender:their|his}}. In French "son peuple" refers back to "cette personne" or "quelqu'un" in ordinary generic French, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: "kuitia unajisi" (profane)
decisions.reason: "Kuitia unajisi" is to treat a holy thing as common, the sense of the verb (m1); Readable says what that means, "kuichukulia kama siku ya kawaida", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "자기 백성 가운데서 끊어지다" (L, B); "백성 가운데서 끊어져야 한다" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "cut off" is kept as "끊어지다" at every level, since the meaning decision leaves open how the person was removed (death or exclusion); "쫓겨나다" would settle it as exile. The Korean has no pronoun to put under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: "bị khai trừ khỏi dân mình" (Literal, Balanced); "bị loại ra khỏi dân chúng" (Readable)
decisions.reason: Keeps the picture of being cut off from the people (meaning decision) without saying how; "khai trừ" is the formal word, and Readable uses a plainer one.

decisions.choice: será cortada (L), será eliminado (B) do meio do seu povo; deve ser eliminado do povo (R); certamente será morto (L), deverá ser morto (B), tem de ser morto (R); no gender setting
decisions.reason: "Quem" and "essa pessoa" already include everyone, and the "seu" that refers back to them is ordinary generic Portuguese, so the gender setting the English needs for "their / his" has nothing to change, as at 30:33. "Cut off" (m3) and the death penalty (m2) follow the book's decisions at 12:15 and 19:12: "cortada" at Literal and "eliminado" at Balanced and Readable; "certamente será morto", "deverá ser morto", "tem de ser morto".

decisions.choice: no gender span on "ከሕዝቡ"
decisions.reason: The Amharic possessive is generic here and includes women, so the English span ("their"/"his") has no Amharic counterpart.

decisions.choice: የሚያቃልለው ("whoever treats it as common")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb here (ḥalal) means to treat a holy thing as common, not to make it ritually unclean (ṭameʾ). The Amharic Pentateuch keeps ማቃለል for the first and ማርከስ for the second, as Leviticus does throughout; Readable says the same plainly: እንደ ተራ ቀን የሚቆጥረው.

decisions.choice: "अपने लोगों" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span on the pronoun, as the English "their / his"
decisions.reason: Hindi "अपने" (one's own) does not mark gender, so the law reads as applying to anyone without a span, as in 30:33.

decisions.choice: "народа своего", no gender span
alternatives: a span as in the English "their / his"
decisions.reason: The English has a gender span on "their / his people"; Russian uses the reflexive "свой", which does not mark gender, so it needs no span. "Душа" (L) keeps the Hebrew "that person" (literally soul).

decisions.choice: mot yumat: "必ず死刑に処せられる" (L, B), "死刑にされなければならない" (R)
decisions.reason: The death penalty, stated firmly (m2).

decisions.choice: "その民" / "自分の民" with no gender span for the English {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: Japanese is already inclusive here, as at 30:33.

source.text: שֵׁ֣שֶׁת יָמִים֮ יֵעָשֶׂ֣ה מְלָאכָה֒ וּבַיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י שַׁבַּ֧ת שַׁבָּת֛וֹן קֹ֖דֶשׁ לַיהוָ֑ה כָּל־הָעֹשֶׂ֧ה מְלָאכָ֛ה בְּי֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֖ת מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: Six days will be done work, and on the day the seventh [is] a sabbath of sabbath rest, holy to Yahweh; every one who does work on [the] day of the sabbath surely shall be put to death.

en.L: Six days work shall be done, but on the seventh day [is] a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Whoever does work on the Sabbath day shall surely be put to death.
en.B: There are six days in which work may be done. The seventh day, though, is a Sabbath of full rest, set apart as holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Anyone who works on the Sabbath day must be put to death.
en.R: You may work for six days. But the seventh day is a day of complete rest. It belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Anyone who works on that day must be put to death.

es.L: Seis días se hará trabajo, pero el día séptimo [es] sábado de reposo completo, santo para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Cualquiera que haga trabajo en el día del sábado, sin falta se le dará muerte.
es.B: Hay seis días en que se puede trabajar. Pero el séptimo día es sábado de reposo total, apartado como santo para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Cualquiera que trabaje en el día sábado será condenado a muerte.
es.R: {{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} trabajar durante seis días. Pero el séptimo día es un día de descanso completo. Pertenece {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. El que trabaje ese día debe ser condenado a muerte.

fr.L: Six jours on fera le travail, mais le septième jour [est] un sabbat de repos complet, saint pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Quiconque fera un travail le jour du sabbat sera certainement mis à mort.
fr.B: Il y a six jours pour travailler. Mais le septième jour est un sabbat de repos total, consacré {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. Quiconque travaillera le jour du sabbat sera mis à mort.
fr.R: Vous pouvez travailler pendant six jours. Mais le septième jour est un jour de repos complet. Il appartient {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. Celui qui travaille ce jour-là doit être mis à mort.

sw.L: Siku sita kazi itafanywa, lakini siku ya saba [ni] Sabato ya pumziko kamili, takatifu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Kila afanyaye kazi siku ya Sabato kwa hakika atauawa.
sw.B: Kuna siku sita za kufanya kazi. Lakini siku ya saba ni Sabato ya pumziko kamili, iliyotengwa kuwa takatifu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Mtu yeyote atakayefanya kazi siku ya Sabato atauawa.
sw.R: Mnaweza kufanya kazi kwa siku sita. Lakini siku ya saba ni siku ya kupumzika kabisa. Ni ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Mtu yeyote anayefanya kazi siku hiyo lazima auawe.

vi.L: Sáu ngày [thì] làm công việc, nhưng ngày thứ bảy [là] ngày Sa-bát nghỉ ngơi hoàn toàn, thánh cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Ai làm việc trong ngày Sa-bát chắc chắn phải bị xử tử.
vi.B: Có sáu ngày để làm việc, còn ngày thứ bảy là ngày Sa-bát, ngày nghỉ ngơi trọn vẹn, được biệt riêng làm ngày thánh cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Ai làm việc trong ngày Sa-bát phải bị xử tử.
vi.R: Các ngươi được làm việc trong sáu ngày. Nhưng ngày thứ bảy là ngày nghỉ ngơi hoàn toàn. Ngày ấy thuộc về {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Ai làm việc trong ngày ấy phải bị xử tử.

ko.L: 엿새 동안은 일을 할 것이나, 일곱째 날은 완전한 쉼의 안식일이요, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 거룩하다. 안식일에 일을 하는 자는 누구든지 반드시 죽임을 당할 것이다.
ko.B: 엿새 동안은 일을 할 수 있다. 그러나 일곱째 날은 완전히 쉬는 안식일이며, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 바친 거룩한 날이다. 누구든지 안식일에 일을 하면 반드시 죽여야 한다.
ko.R: 엿새 동안은 일을 해도 된다. 그러나 일곱째 날은 완전히 쉬는 날이다. 그날은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 속한 날이다. 그날에 일하는 사람은 죽여야 한다.

pt.L: Seis dias se fará trabalho, mas no sétimo dia [é] sábado de descanso solene, santo {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}. Quem fizer trabalho no dia do sábado certamente será morto.
pt.B: Há seis dias em que se pode trabalhar. O sétimo dia, porém, é um sábado de descanso solene, consagrado {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}. Quem trabalhar no dia de sábado deverá ser morto.
pt.R: Vocês podem trabalhar durante seis dias. Mas o sétimo dia é um dia de descanso completo. Ele pertence {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}. Quem trabalhar nesse dia tem de ser morto.

am.L: ስድስት ቀን ሥራ ይሠራል፤ በሰባተኛው ቀን ግን {{divine_name:ለእግዚአብሔር|ለያህዌ}} የተቀደሰ የፍጹም ዕረፍት ሰንበት ነው፤ በሰንበት ቀን ሥራ የሚሠራ ሁሉ ፈጽሞ ይገደል።
am.B: ሥራ የሚሠራባቸው ስድስት ቀኖች አሉ። ሰባተኛው ቀን ግን {{divine_name:ለእግዚአብሔር|ለያህዌ}} የተቀደሰ፣ የፍጹም ዕረፍት ሰንበት ነው። በሰንበት ቀን የሚሠራ ማንም ሰው ይገደል።
am.R: ለስድስት ቀን መሥራት ትችላላችሁ። ሰባተኛው ቀን ግን የፍጹም ዕረፍት ቀን ነው። {{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} ነው። በዚያ ቀን የሚሠራ ማንም ሰው መገደል አለበት።

hi.L: छह दिन काम किया जाए, परंतु सातवें दिन पूर्ण विश्राम का सब्त [है], {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के लिए पवित्र। जो कोई सब्त के दिन काम करे वह निश्चय मार डाला जाए।
hi.B: छह दिन काम किया जा सकता है। परंतु सातवाँ दिन पूर्ण विश्राम का सब्त है, जो {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के लिए पवित्र है। जो कोई सब्त के दिन काम करे, वह मार डाला जाए।
hi.R: तुम छह दिन काम कर सकते हो। पर सातवाँ दिन पूरे आराम का दिन है। वह {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} का है। जो कोई उस दिन काम करे, उसे मार डाला जाए।

ru.L: Шесть дней пусть делается работа, а в седьмой день — суббота полного покоя, святыня {{divine_name:ГОСПОДУ|Яхве}}. Всякий, кто делает работу в день субботний, непременно будет предан смерти.
ru.B: Шесть дней можно работать. А седьмой день — суббота полного покоя, посвящённая {{divine_name:ГОСПОДУ|Яхве}}. Всякий, кто будет работать в субботний день, должен быть предан смерти.
ru.R: Работать можно шесть дней. Но седьмой день — день полного отдыха. Он принадлежит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДУ|Яхве}}. Кто будет работать в этот день, должен быть предан смерти.

ja.L: 六日の間は仕事がなされるが、第七の日は全き休みの安息日であり、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}にとって聖なるものである。安息日に仕事をする者はだれでも、必ず死刑に処せられる。
ja.B: 仕事をしてよいのは六日間である。しかし七日目は完全な休みの安息日であり、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}のための聖なる日である。安息日に仕事をする者はだれでも、必ず死刑に処せられる。
ja.R: 六日の間は働いてもよい。しかし、七日目は完全に休む日である。その日は{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}のものである。その日に仕事をする者は、死刑にされなければならない。

uk.L: Шість днів робитиметься робота, а сьомого дня — субота повного спочинку, свята {{divine_name:ГОСПОДУ|Ягве}}. Кожен, хто робитиме роботу в день суботній, неодмінно буде скараний на смерть.
uk.B: Є шість днів, у які можна працювати. Але сьомий день — субота повного спочинку, відділена як свята для {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}. Кожного, хто працюватиме в суботній день, треба скарати на смерть.
uk.R: Шість днів можете працювати. Але сьомий день — день повного відпочинку. Він належить {{divine_name:ГОСПОДУ|Ягве}}. Кожного, хто працюватиме того дня, треба скарати на смерть.

decisions.choice: a Sabbath of complete rest: the fullest rest
decisions.reason: The noun is followed by a longer form of the same word to make it as strong as possible, a rest from all work. The phrase first appears in 16:23 and is used again of the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:31).

decisions.choice: holy to Yahweh: belonging to God
decisions.reason: The day is holy to the people (verse 14) because it is first holy to God, set apart as his (20:10).

decisions.choice: It belongs to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says what "holy to the LORD" means (m2).

decisions.choice: sábado de descanso solene (L, B); dia de descanso completo (R)
decisions.reason: The doubled Hebrew word means the fullest rest (m1). Literal and Balanced say "descanso solene", as the book first did at 16:23; Readable says "descanso completo", as the English Readable says "complete rest".

decisions.choice: shabbat shabbaton: "全き休みの安息日" (L), "完全な休みの安息日" (B), "完全に休む日" (R)
decisions.reason: The fullest rest (m1).

source.text: וְשָׁמְר֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶת־הַשַּׁבָּ֑ת לַעֲשׂ֧וֹת אֶת־הַשַּׁבָּ֛ת לְדֹרֹתָ֖ם בְּרִ֥ית עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And shall keep [the] sons of Israel the sabbath, to do the sabbath throughout their generations [as] a covenant of perpetuity.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, observing the Sabbath throughout their generations [as] a perpetual covenant.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} are to keep the Sabbath, holding to it generation after generation as a covenant for all time.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} must keep the Sabbath day in every generation. It is a covenant that will last forever.

es.L: Y los hijos de Israel guardarán el sábado, celebrando el sábado por sus generaciones [como] pacto perpetuo.
es.B: Los israelitas guardarán el sábado y lo observarán de generación en generación como un pacto para siempre.
es.R: Los israelitas deben guardar el sábado en cada generación. Es un pacto que durará para siempre.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël garderont le sabbat, en observant le sabbat au long de leurs générations [comme] une alliance perpétuelle.
fr.B: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} garderont le sabbat et l’observeront de génération en génération, comme une alliance pour toujours.
fr.R: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} doivent respecter le jour du sabbat dans chaque génération. C’est une alliance qui durera toujours.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wataishika Sabato, wakiiadhimisha Sabato katika vizazi vyao vyote [kuwa] agano la milele.
sw.B: Waisraeli waishike Sabato, wakiiadhimisha kizazi hadi kizazi kama agano la kudumu milele.
sw.R: Waisraeli lazima waishike siku ya Sabato katika kila kizazi. Ni agano litakalodumu milele.

vi.L: Con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên phải giữ ngày Sa-bát, giữ ngày Sa-bát qua các thế hệ của họ [như] một giao ước đời đời.
vi.B: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên phải giữ ngày Sa-bát, gìn giữ ngày ấy từ thế hệ này sang thế hệ khác như một giao ước đời đời.
vi.R: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên phải giữ ngày Sa-bát trong mọi thế hệ. Đó là một giao ước sẽ còn mãi mãi.

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘 자손은 안식일을 지켜, 대대로 안식일을 영원한 언약으로 지킬 것이다.
ko.B: 이스라엘 백성은 안식일을 지켜야 한다. 대대로 안식일을 영원한 언약으로 지켜야 한다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 사람들은 대대로 안식일을 지켜야 한다. 이것은 영원히 이어질 언약이다.

pt.L: E os filhos de Israel guardarão o sábado, celebrando o sábado pelas suas gerações [como] aliança perpétua.
pt.B: Os israelitas guardarão o sábado, observando-o de geração em geração como uma aliança para sempre.
pt.R: Os israelitas devem guardar o sábado em todas as gerações. Ele é uma aliança que vai durar para sempre.

decisions.choice: a perpetual covenant: a covenant that lasts for all time
decisions.reason: The Sabbath is itself called a covenant, the part Israel keeps of the covenant God made at Sinai. It is to last as long as Israel lasts, like the "perpetual covenant" with Noah (Genesis 9:16).

decisions.choice: to do the Sabbath: to observe it
decisions.reason: To "do" the Sabbath means to keep it as God commanded (Deuteronomy 5:15). The same verb was used of doing work in verses 14-15.

decisions.choice: for all time
decisions.reason: As with "a statute for all time" elsewhere in Exodus. Literal says "perpetual".

decisions.choice: aliança perpétua (L); uma aliança para sempre (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Aliança" is the book's word for covenant (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md); Literal says "perpétua", as with "estatuto perpétuo", and Balanced and Readable "para sempre". The "filhos de Israel" take no gender setting (1:7).

decisions.choice: in six days Yahweh made the heavens and the earth: the reason for the Sabbath
decisions.reason: The reason looks back to creation, as the Sabbath command does in 20:11 (Genesis 2:1-3). The verb "rested" is the root of "Sabbath": God ceased from his work.

decisions.choice: took breath: God was refreshed, a bold human picture
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for breath or life and means to catch one's breath, to be refreshed after labor. It is used of a tired servant and a foreigner resting on the Sabbath (23:12) and of David's weary men (2 Samuel 16:14). Said of God it is a bold picture: God rests like a worker at the end of the week. It does not mean God grew tired (Isaiah 40:28); it shows his pleasure in finished work and sets the pattern for his people's rest.

decisions.choice: took breath (Literal); was refreshed (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of drawing breath. Balanced and Readable say "was refreshed", the wording of the King James Version, which keeps the sense without suggesting that God was out of breath. "Caught his breath" was considered; it is vivid but could suggest exhaustion (m2).

decisions.choice: the sky
decisions.reason: Readable says "the sky" for "the heavens", as in Genesis 1.

decisions.choice: "tomó aliento" (L); "se recreó" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Recrearse" means to be refreshed and to take delight, without suggesting that God was worn out (m2); "cobrar aliento" would suggest exhaustion. Literal keeps the picture of breath.

decisions.choice: "a repris haleine" (L); "a goûté le repos" (B, R)
decisions.reason: French has no neutral word for "was refreshed": "reprendre des forces" would say that God had grown tired, which the English decision avoids (m2), and "se rafraîchir" means to cool down. "Goûter le repos" says that God rested and took pleasure in it. Literal keeps the picture of breath.

decisions.choice: "kuvuta pumzi" (L); "akaburudika" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Kuburudika" is to be refreshed and at ease, without suggesting that God had grown weak (m2). Literal keeps the picture of drawing breath.

decisions.choice: "숨을 돌리셨다" (L); "새 힘을 얻으셨다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "took breath" is a bold human picture (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the picture with the idiom "숨을 돌리다", Balanced and Readable say what it means, as the English "was refreshed" does.

decisions.choice: "lấy hơi lại" (Literal); "được tươi tỉnh lại" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of drawing breath; the other levels say what it means, as the English does (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: tomou fôlego (L); se revigorou (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of drawing breath (m2), as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable say "se revigorou", refreshed, which keeps the sense without suggesting that God was out of breath. "Os céus e a terra" follows Genesis 1:1 in Portuguese; Readable says "o céu", as the English Readable says "the sky".

decisions.choice: "ተነፈሰ" (L); "ታደሰ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the bold picture "took breath"; Balanced and Readable say "was refreshed", as the English levels do.

decisions.choice: "почил и перевёл дух" (L); "отдохнул" (B), "набрался сил" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of drawing breath (m2); Balanced and Readable give its sense, as the English does.

decisions.choice: No respect forms for YHWH here ("造り", "休み"), since God speaks of himself
decisions.reason: As in chapters 9 and 11: God naming himself inside his own words uses plain verbs.

decisions.choice: vayyinnafash: "息をついた" (L), "憩った" (B), "元気を取り戻した" (R)

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה כְּכַלֹּתוֹ֙ לְדַבֵּ֤ר אִתּוֹ֙ בְּהַ֣ר סִינַ֔י שְׁנֵ֖י לֻחֹ֣ת הָעֵדֻ֑ת לֻחֹ֣ת אֶ֔בֶן כְּתֻבִ֖ים בְּאֶצְבַּ֥ע אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he gave to Moses, when he finished speaking with him on [the] mountain of Sinai, [the] two tablets of the testimony, tablets of stone, written by [the] finger of God.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave to Moses, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had finished speaking with him on Mount Sinai, the two tablets of the testimony, tablets of stone, written by the finger of God.
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} handed him the two tablets of the testimony, stone tablets written by the finger of God.
en.R: When God finished talking with Moses on Mount Sinai, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave Moses the two stone tablets of the covenant. God had written on them with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own finger.

es.L: Y dio a Moisés, cuando acabó de hablar con él en el monte Sinaí, las dos tablas del Testimonio, tablas de piedra, escritas por el dedo de Dios.
es.B: Cuando terminó de hablar con Moisés en el monte Sinaí, le dio las dos tablas del Testimonio, tablas de piedra grabadas por el dedo de Dios.
es.R: Cuando Dios terminó de hablar con Moisés en el monte Sinaí, le dio las dos tablas de piedra del pacto. Dios había escrito en ellas con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio dedo.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donna à Moïse, quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} eut achevé de parler avec lui sur le mont Sinaï, les deux tables du Témoignage, tables de pierre, écrites par le doigt de Dieu.
fr.B: Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} eut fini de parler avec Moïse sur le mont Sinaï, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui donna les deux tables du Témoignage, tables de pierre gravées par le doigt de Dieu.
fr.R: Quand Dieu a fini de parler avec Moïse sur le mont Sinaï, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui a donné les deux tables de pierre de l’alliance. Dieu avait écrit dessus de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre doigt.

sw.L: Naye akampa Musa, alipomaliza kusema naye juu ya mlima Sinai, vibao viwili vya Ushuhuda, vibao vya mawe, vilivyoandikwa kwa kidole cha Mungu.
sw.B: Alipomaliza kusema na Musa juu ya mlima Sinai, akampa vibao viwili vya Ushuhuda, vibao vya mawe vilivyoandikwa kwa kidole cha Mungu.
sw.R: Mungu alipomaliza kuzungumza na Musa juu ya mlima Sinai, alimpa Musa vibao viwili vya mawe vya agano. Mungu alikuwa ameandika juu yake kwa kidole {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} mwenyewe.

vi.L: Ngài ban cho Môi-se, khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán xong với người trên núi Si-na-i, hai bảng chứng ước, [là] các bảng bằng đá, được viết bởi ngón tay của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Khi đã phán xong với Môi-se trên núi Si-na-i, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban cho người hai bảng chứng ước, là các bảng bằng đá do chính ngón tay Đức Chúa Trời viết.
vi.R: Khi Đức Chúa Trời phán xong với Môi-se trên núi Si-na-i, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trao cho Môi-se hai bảng đá giao ước. Chính Đức Chúa Trời đã dùng ngón tay của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} viết trên đó.

ko.L: 그리고 그분께서 시내 산에서 모세와 말씀하시기를 마치셨을 때, 증거판 둘, 곧 하나님의 손가락으로 쓰신 돌판들을 모세에게 주셨다.
ko.B: 하나님께서는 시내 산에서 모세에게 하실 말씀을 다 마치신 뒤, 증거판 두 개를 그에게 주셨다. 그것은 하나님께서 손가락으로 친히 쓰신 돌판이었다.
ko.R: 하나님께서는 시내 산에서 모세와 이야기를 다 마치시고, 언약을 새긴 돌판 두 개를 모세에게 주셨다. 그 돌판에는 하나님께서 손가락으로 직접 글을 쓰셨다.

pt.L: E deu a Moisés, quando acabou de falar com ele no monte Sinai, as duas tábuas do Testemunho, tábuas de pedra, escritas pelo dedo de Deus.
pt.B: Quando acabou de falar com Moisés no monte Sinai, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhe deu as duas tábuas do Testemunho, tábuas de pedra escritas pelo dedo de Deus.
pt.R: Quando Deus terminou de falar com Moisés no monte Sinai, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} deu a Moisés as duas tábuas de pedra da aliança. Deus tinha escrito nelas com o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} próprio dedo.

am.L: ከእርሱም ጋር በሲና ተራራ ላይ መነጋገሩን በፈጸመ ጊዜ፣ ለሙሴ ሁለቱን የምስክሩን ጽላቶች፣ በእግዚአብሔር ጣት የተጻፉ የድንጋይ ጽላቶችን ሰጠው።
am.B: በሲና ተራራ ላይ ከሙሴ ጋር መነጋገሩን በፈጸመ ጊዜ ሁለቱን የምስክሩን ጽላቶች፣ በእግዚአብሔር ጣት የተቀረጹትን የድንጋይ ጽላቶች ሰጠው።
am.R: እግዚአብሔር በሲና ተራራ ላይ ከሙሴ ጋር መነጋገሩን በጨረሰ ጊዜ ሁለቱን የቃል ኪዳኑን የድንጋይ ጽላቶች ለሙሴ ሰጠው። እግዚአብሔር በራሱ ጣት ጽፎባቸው ነበር።

hi.L: और जब उन्होंने सीनै पहाड़ पर मूसा से बात करना समाप्त किया, तब उन्होंने मूसा को साक्षी-पत्र की दो पटियाएँ दीं, पत्थर की पटियाएँ, जो परमेश्वर की उँगली से लिखी हुई थीं।
hi.B: जब परमेश्वर सीनै पहाड़ पर मूसा से बात कर चुके, तब उन्होंने उसे साक्षी-पत्र की दो पटियाएँ दीं, पत्थर की पटियाएँ, जिन पर परमेश्वर की उँगली से लिखा गया था।
hi.R: जब परमेश्वर सीनै पहाड़ पर मूसा से बात कर चुके, तब उन्होंने मूसा को वाचा की पत्थर की दो पटियाएँ दीं। परमेश्वर ने अपनी ही उँगली से उन पर लिखा था।

ru.L: И {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} дал Моисею, когда окончил говорить с ним на горе Синай, две скрижали свидетельства, скрижали каменные, написанные перстом Божьим.
ru.B: Окончив говорить с Моисеем на горе Синай, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} дал ему две скрижали свидетельства, каменные скрижали, написанные перстом Божьим.
ru.R: Когда Бог закончил говорить с Моисеем на горе Синай, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} дал Моисею две каменные доски завета. Бог написал на них своим собственным пальцем.

ja.L: そして[神は]シナイ山でモーセと語り終えられたとき、証しの二枚の板、すなわち神の指で書かれた石の板を、モーセに授けられた。
ja.B: シナイ山でモーセと語り終えられると、証しの板二枚をモーセに授けられた。それは、神の指で記された石の板であった。
ja.R: 神は、シナイ山でモーセと話し終えられると、石でできた二枚の契約の板をモーセにお与えになりました。神は、ご自分の指でその板に文字を書かれたのでした。

uk.L: І дав {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} Мойсеєві, коли закінчив говорити з ним на горі Синай, дві таблиці свідчення, камʼяні таблиці, написані пальцем Божим.
uk.B: Коли {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} закінчив говорити з Мойсеєм на горі Синай, {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} дав йому дві таблиці свідчення, камʼяні таблиці, написані пальцем Божим.
uk.R: Коли Бог закінчив розмову з Мойсеєм на горі Синай, {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} дав Мойсеєві дві камʼяні таблиці завіту. Бог написав на них власним пальцем.

decisions.choice: the two tablets of the testimony: the stone tablets bearing the covenant
decisions.reason: These are the tablets God promised in 24:12, to be placed in the ark (25:16). They bear the words of the covenant, the Ten Words (34:28), as God's witness to it. Moses will break them in 32:19, and God will write them again (34:1).

decisions.choice: written by the finger of God: written by God himself
decisions.reason: The finger stands for God's own direct action, as when Pharaoh's magicians said "This is the finger of God" (8:15). The tablets were "the work of God" and the writing "the writing of God" (32:16).

decisions.choice: God ... of the covenant ... his own finger
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the subject, calls the tablets "of the covenant" for "of the testimony" (m1), and adds "own" to bring out that God himself wrote them (m2).

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The English has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} for God. Spanish leaves the subject in the verb ("dio", "acabó"), so there is no word for the span to sit on.

decisions.choice: "증거판" (L, B); "언약을 새긴 돌판" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch term sheet: the tablets of the testimony are "증거판"; Readable says what they were, as the English Readable says "the stone tablets of the covenant". Korean names God ("하나님께서") in Balanced where English uses a pronoun, since Korean avoids a bare pronoun for God.

decisions.choice: "hai bảng chứng ước" (Literal, Balanced); "hai bảng đá giao ước" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's word for the tablets of the testimony; Readable says what they hold, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: as duas tábuas do Testemunho (L, B); as duas tábuas de pedra da aliança (R)
decisions.reason: The stone tablets themselves are "tábuas" at every level, the word chapter 32 uses for them (32:15-16), and "o Testemunho" keeps its capital (25:16); Readable says "da aliança", as the English Readable does. Where Readable explains "the testimony" alone it says "as tábuas da aliança" (16:34). Literal leaves the subject unexpressed, as the Hebrew does, since Portuguese can, and "ele" there is Moses.

decisions.choice: "ጽላቶች" (tablets); "የምስክሩ ጽላቶች" (L, B), "የቃል ኪዳኑ ጽላቶች" (R)
decisions.reason: "ጽላት" is the established word for the stone tablets; Readable names the testimony as the covenant, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: The subject is shown by the respect forms ("授けられた"), with "[神は]" at Literal and "神は" at Readable; Balanced names no subject
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves God unnamed until "the finger of God"; Japanese avoids a pronoun for God.
